- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment or price — apply lagged smoothing: reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if sentiment peaks within 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 2–5% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum — if sentiment turns positive after day 15–20, increase forecast tail end by 2–5% to capture rally.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative swings, model tends to underestimate lows — adjust forecast downward by 3–5% for early period if sentiment is weak.
